name: Critical minerals
summary: China's rare-earth export-control pause expires 10 Nov with no renewal published
state: China's one-year suspension of its expanded October 2025 rare-earth export controls expires on 10 Nov, and no formal renewal had been published as of 7 Nov (Mining Technology; FXStreet). Lapsed controls would bring back tighter licensing. No production stoppages outside China have been confirmed, so the Alert line is not crossed.
for_you: Manufacturers relying on Chinese rare earths, such as carmakers and electronics firms, are most exposed.
rubric_hit: Export controls pending re-imposition = Watch; no stoppages outside China (Alert)

sources.title: Mining Technology — China rare earth export pause nears expiry
FXStreet — China's rare earth leverage has an expiration date: 10 November

why: Rare earths, gallium, germanium and graphite are chokepoints for chips, EVs and defence — and China dominates processing.
drivers: Export controls, trade disputes, mine outages, stockpiling.

rubric.alert: Export bans in force that are causing reported production stoppages outside China.
rubric.watch: New export controls announced or licensing slowed.
rubric.normal: No new export restrictions in the past month.
